title: The Problem is You Suck
description: A deliberately abrasive lesson argues that improvement requires admitting ignorance, practicing everywhere like Keith Haring, approaching galleries before permission feels earned and valuing the learner who researches gaps over the person who pretends expertise.
summary: A deliberately abrasive lesson argues that improvement requires admitting ignorance, practicing everywhere like Keith Haring, approaching galleries before permission feels earned and valuing the learner who researches gaps over the person who pretends expertise. This is an official-channel creative lesson or reflection, not clinical treatment or a universal formula. Its chronological map follows the route's own transcript and distinguishes art-making instructions from autobiographical claims, jokes and metaphors. Visually dependent technique still requires the source video.
